Option D (Long-running job execution (up to 24 hours)) is incorrect; Lambda functions have a maximum execution duration of 15 minutes. Option E (Direct integration with Apache Kafka clusters) is not a primary, built-in benefit; while Lambda can process data from MSK, it's not a direct 'built-in support' in the same way as its core scaling and billing model.

text: A data engineer needs to optimize SQL queries for an Amazon Redshift data warehouse to improve performance for analytical workloads. Which of these practices are effective for SQL query optimization in Redshift? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Using `SELECT *` for all queries to simplify development","Employing `VACUUM` and `ANALYZE` regularly","Designing tables with appropriate distribution and sort keys","Running queries during peak business hours to ensure fresh data","Disabling query caching to always fetch new data"]
explanation: Option B (Employing `VACUUM` and `ANALYZE` regularly) is crucial for Redshift performance. `VACUUM` reclaims space and sorts rows, while `ANALYZE` updates table statistics, which the query optimizer uses to create efficient execution plans. Option C (Designing tables with appropriate distribution and sort keys) is fundamental for Redshift optimization. Distribution keys determine how data is spread across compute nodes, and sort keys determine the order in which data is stored within blocks, both significantly impacting query performance. Option A (Using `SELECT *` for all queries to simplify development) is an anti-pattern; it retrieves unnecessary columns, increasing I/O and network traffic, which degrades performance. Option D (Running queries during peak business hours to ensure fresh data) is not an optimization practice; while data freshness is important, running heavy queries during peak hours can contend for resources and slow down other critical workloads. Option E (Disabling query caching to always fetch new data) is incorrect; query caching (e.g., in Redshift Spectrum or other tools) can significantly speed up repeated queries on unchanged data, and disabling it would generally hurt performance.

text: When developing data pipelines using AWS Lambda, which aspects are crucial for managing and optimizing the function's performance and cost? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Configuring the allocated memory for the function","Choosing the appropriate runtime environment (e.g., Python, Node.js)","Increasing the maximum execution timeout to 24 hours","Manually provisioning underlying EC2 instances","Setting up a dedicated Amazon RDS instance for logging"]
explanation: Option A (Configuring the allocated memory for the function) is critical because Lambda allocates CPU proportionally to memory. Increasing memory can improve performance for compute-intensive tasks, but also increases cost. Finding the right balance is key. Option B (Choosing the appropriate runtime environment) is important as different runtimes have varying startup times and performance characteristics, impacting cold starts and overall execution speed. Option C (Increasing the maximum execution timeout to 24 hours) is incorrect; Lambda functions have a maximum timeout of 15 minutes, not 24 hours. Option D (Manually provisioning underlying EC2 instances) is incorrect; Lambda is a serverless service, meaning AWS manages the underlying compute infrastructure, and users do not provision EC2 instances. Option E (Setting up a dedicated Amazon RDS instance for logging) is incorrect; Lambda automatically integrates with Amazon CloudWatch Logs for logging, and setting up a dedicated RDS instance for this purpose would be unnecessary and introduce additional operational overhead.

text: A data engineer is using AWS CloudFormation to deploy a serverless data processing pipeline that includes AWS Lambda functions, Amazon S3 buckets, and AWS Step Functions state machines. Which of the following are benefits of using CloudFormation for this purpose? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Enables manual resource provisioning for fine-grained control","Provides a single source of truth for infrastructure definition","Facilitates consistent and repeatable deployments across environments","Automatically optimizes SQL queries within Lambda functions","Offers built-in version control for application code"]
explanation: Option B (Provides a single source of truth for infrastructure definition) is a major benefit of CloudFormation, as it allows all infrastructure resources to be defined in a single, version-controlled template. Option C (Facilitates consistent and repeatable deployments across environments) ensures that the same infrastructure can be deployed reliably in development, testing, and production environments, reducing configuration drift and errors. Option A (Enables manual resource provisioning for fine-grained control) is incorrect; CloudFormation automates resource provisioning, moving away from manual processes. Option D (Automatically optimizes SQL queries within Lambda functions) is incorrect; CloudFormation manages infrastructure, not application-level code optimization. Option E (Offers built-in version control for application code) is incorrect; while CloudFormation templates can be version-controlled (e.g., in Git), it does not provide built-in version control for the application code itself (e.g., Lambda function code), which typically resides in a separate repository.

text: A data engineer is setting up a Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline for AWS Glue ETL jobs. Which of these practices are essential for ensuring a robust and efficient CI/CD process for data pipelines? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Manually deploying Glue jobs to production after each code change","Automating unit and integration tests for Glue job scripts","Using version control (e.g., Git) for Glue job code","Skipping schema validation to speed up deployments","Relying solely on manual approval for all pipeline stages"]
explanation: Option B (Automating unit and integration tests for Glue job scripts) is essential for CI/CD, as automated tests catch errors early, ensuring code quality and preventing regressions before deployment. Option C (Using version control (e.g., Git) for Glue job code) is fundamental for any CI/CD process, providing a single source of truth, enabling collaboration, tracking changes, and facilitating rollbacks. Option A (Manually deploying Glue jobs to production after each code change) defeats the purpose of CI/CD, which aims to automate deployments for speed and consistency. Option D (Skipping schema validation to speed up deployments) is an anti-pattern; schema validation is crucial in data pipelines to prevent data quality issues and job failures due to unexpected data formats. Option E (Relying solely on manual approval for all pipeline stages) can introduce bottlenecks and slow down the deployment process; while manual approvals might be necessary for critical production stages, automating as much as possible is a core tenet of CI/CD.

text: Which AWS services can be used to package and deploy serverless applications, including AWS Lambda functions and AWS Step Functions state machines, as part of a data pipeline? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM)","AWS Elastic Beanstalk","AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK)","Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling","AWS Data Pipeline"]
explanation: Option A (AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM)) is an open-source framework for building serverless applications. It provides a shorthand syntax to define Lambda functions, API Gateway APIs, DynamoDB tables, and Step Functions state machines, which are then transformed into CloudFormation templates for deployment. Option C (AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK)) allows developers to define cloud infrastructure using familiar programming languages and then synthesize it into CloudFormation templates, making it suitable for packaging and deploying serverless applications. Option B (AWS Elastic Beanstalk) is a service for deploying and scaling web applications and services developed with various programming languages, but it's not specifically designed for serverless components like Lambda and Step Functions. Option D (Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling) is used to automatically adjust the number of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group, which is not relevant for packaging and deploying serverless applications. Option E (AWS Data Pipeline) is a legacy service for orchestrating data workflows, but it's not used for packaging and deploying serverless applications themselves.

text: A data engineer is optimizing a PySpark script running on AWS Glue for processing large datasets. Which of the following techniques can help improve the performance of the Glue ETL job? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Increasing the number of Data Processing Units (DPUs)","Disabling data partitioning for faster writes to S3","Using `SELECT *` in SQL queries within the script","Optimizing data formats (e.g., converting to Parquet)","Reducing the allocated memory for executors"]
explanation: Option A (Increasing the number of Data Processing Units (DPUs)) provides more compute resources (executors and memory) to the Glue job, allowing for greater parallelism and faster processing of large datasets. Option D (Optimizing data formats (e.g., converting to Parquet)) is a crucial optimization. Columnar formats like Apache Parquet are highly efficient for analytical queries, reducing I/O and improving query performance compared to row-based formats like CSV. Option B (Disabling data partitioning for faster writes to S3) is an anti-pattern (`ap-1.2-002`); while it might seem faster for writes, it leads to full table scans for subsequent reads, drastically increasing query costs and time in services like Athena or Redshift Spectrum. Option C (Using `SELECT *` in SQL queries within the script) is an anti-pattern; it retrieves unnecessary data, increasing I/O and processing overhead. Option E (Reducing the allocated memory for executors) would likely degrade performance, especially for memory-intensive Spark operations, potentially leading to out-of-memory errors or slower execution.

text: A data processing job running on AWS Lambda frequently times out when processing large datasets, even with the maximum memory allocated. The team wants to optimize the job's runtime and ensure it completes reliably. Which two strategies should the data engineer consider to address this issue? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Refactor the job to use a distributed processing framework like AWS Glue or Amazon EMR.","Increase the Lambda function's timeout setting to the maximum allowed 15 minutes.","Optimize the SQL queries within the Lambda function for better performance.","Split the large dataset into smaller chunks and process them in parallel using multiple Lambda invocations.","Migrate the Lambda function to an Amazon EC2 instance for more compute power."]
explanation: Option A (Refactor the job to use a distributed processing framework like AWS Glue or Amazon EMR) is the most appropriate solution for heavy, long-running ETL transforms over large datasets, as Lambda has a 15-minute timeout and limited memory (ap-1.2-001). These services are designed for large-scale data processing. Option D (Split the large dataset into smaller chunks and process them in parallel using multiple Lambda invocations) can help if the individual chunks can be processed within Lambda's limits, effectively parallelizing the workload and making it suitable for Lambda's serverless model. Option B (Increase the Lambda function's timeout setting to the maximum allowed 15 minutes) might temporarily alleviate the issue but doesn't address the fundamental limitation of Lambda for heavy ETL (ap-1.2-001) and may still result in timeouts for very large datasets. Option C (Optimize the SQL queries within the Lambda function) is good practice but might not be sufficient if the dataset size inherently exceeds Lambda's capabilities. Option E (Migrate the Lambda function to an Amazon EC2 instance) would increase operational overhead significantly, moving away from a serverless approach.

text: Which of these are key benefits of using AWS Cloud Development Kit (CDK) for defining data pipeline infrastructure? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Allows defining infrastructure using familiar programming languages","Requires manual management of underlying EC2 instances","Enables automatic optimization of SQL queries","Provides strong type safety and IDE auto-completion","Exclusively supports YAML for infrastructure definition"]
explanation: Option A (Allows defining infrastructure using familiar programming languages) is a primary benefit of AWS CDK, enabling developers to use Python, TypeScript, Java, C#, or Go to define their cloud resources. Option D (Provides strong type safety and IDE auto-completion) significantly improves developer productivity and reduces errors by leveraging the features of modern programming languages and integrated development environments. Option B (Requires manual management of underlying EC2 instances) is incorrect; CDK, like CloudFormation, abstracts away the underlying infrastructure management. Option C (Enables automatic optimization of SQL queries) is incorrect; CDK is for infrastructure definition, not application-level code optimization. Option E (Exclusively supports YAML for infrastructure definition) is incorrect; CDK synthesizes into CloudFormation templates, which can be YAML or JSON, but the CDK code itself is written in programming languages, not YAML.

text: Which of these are key considerations when optimizing the runtime performance of AWS Lambda functions used in data pipelines? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Minimizing the function's memory allocation to save costs","Using efficient algorithms and data structures in the code","Increasing the function's timeout to the maximum 15 minutes for all tasks","Reducing the size of the deployment package","Avoiding concurrent executions to prevent resource contention"]
explanation: Option B (Using efficient algorithms and data structures in the code) directly impacts the computational efficiency of the Lambda function, leading to faster execution times and lower costs. Option D (Reducing the size of the deployment package) can significantly improve cold start times, as smaller packages download and initialize faster. Option A (Minimizing the function's memory allocation to save costs) can be counterproductive if the function is compute-intensive, as CPU is proportional to memory. It's better to find the optimal memory setting rather than just minimizing it. Option C (Increasing the function's timeout to the maximum 15 minutes for all tasks) is not an optimization; while some tasks might need longer, setting it to the maximum for all tasks can mask inefficiencies and lead to higher costs for functions that could complete faster. Option E (Avoiding concurrent executions to prevent resource contention) is generally incorrect for Lambda, which is designed for high concurrency. Avoiding it would limit scalability and throughput, which is often a primary benefit of using Lambda.

text: A data engineer is tasked with deploying a new version of an AWS Lambda function that performs data validation in a serverless data pipeline. Which of the following AWS services or features can assist in managing the deployment and ensuring minimal downtime? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS CodePipeline","AWS DataSync","AWS Lambda Aliases","Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose","AWS Step Functions"]
explanation: Option A (AWS CodePipeline) is a fully managed continuous delivery service that helps automate release pipelines for fast and reliable application and infrastructure updates. It can orchestrate the deployment of new Lambda function versions. Option C (AWS Lambda Aliases) allows you to point to a specific version of a Lambda function. This enables safe deployments by shifting traffic between two versions (e.g., canary deployments) and easily rolling back if issues arise, minimizing downtime. Option B (AWS DataSync) is a data transfer service, not a deployment management tool. Option D (Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose) is for ingesting and delivering streaming data, not for deploying Lambda functions. Option E (AWS Step Functions) is for orchestrating workflows, and while it can invoke Lambda functions, it's not primarily a deployment management service for the Lambda function itself.

text: Which of these are key advantages of using Git for managing the code of AWS Glue ETL jobs and AWS Lambda functions within a data engineering team? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Enables collaborative development and code sharing","Provides automatic code optimization for PySpark scripts","Facilitates version control and change tracking","Automatically deploys code to production environments","Eliminates the need for testing data transformations"]
explanation: Option A (Enables collaborative development and code sharing) is a core benefit of Git, allowing multiple data engineers to work on the same codebase simultaneously and merge their changes efficiently. Option C (Facilitates version control and change tracking) is fundamental to Git, providing a complete history of code changes, enabling rollbacks, and making it easy to understand who changed what and when. Option B (Provides automatic code optimization for PySpark scripts) is incorrect; Git is a version control system and does not perform code optimization. Option D (Automatically deploys code to production environments) is incorrect; Git is for version control; deployment automation typically involves CI/CD services like AWS CodePipeline. Option E (Eliminates the need for testing data transformations) is a dangerous misconception; version control does not replace the need for thorough testing; in fact, it supports a robust testing strategy.

text: A data engineer needs to ensure that all changes to SQL stored procedures used by an Amazon Redshift cluster are tracked, reviewed, and can be easily rolled back. Which practices are essential for managing these SQL assets? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Storing SQL scripts in a version control system like Git","Applying changes directly to the production database via the console","Using `CREATE OR REPLACE` for all procedure updates without review","Implementing a code review process for SQL changes","Maintaining separate SQL files for each environment (dev, test, prod)"]
explanation: Option A (Storing SQL scripts in a version control system like Git) is crucial for tracking changes, maintaining history, and enabling collaboration and rollbacks for SQL assets. Option D (Implementing a code review process for SQL changes) ensures that SQL scripts are reviewed by peers for correctness, performance, and adherence to best practices before being deployed, reducing errors and improving quality. Option B (Applying changes directly to the production database via the console) is an anti-pattern; it bypasses version control and review processes, leading to inconsistent environments and potential production issues. Option C (Using `CREATE OR REPLACE` for all procedure updates without review) is risky; while `CREATE OR REPLACE` can simplify updates, doing so without proper review and testing can introduce breaking changes or performance regressions. Option E (Maintaining separate SQL files for each environment (dev, test, prod)) is generally an anti-pattern for IaC principles; ideally, the same SQL script should be parameterized for different environments, rather than having entirely separate, potentially divergent files.

text: Which of the following are characteristics of AWS Lambda functions that make them suitable for event-driven, lightweight data transformations in a data pipeline? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Supports long-running batch jobs exceeding 15 minutes","Scales automatically with incoming events","Offers a pay-per-execution billing model","Requires manual provisioning of server infrastructure","Optimized for complex, distributed Spark processing"]
explanation: Option B (Scales automatically with incoming events) is a core characteristic of AWS Lambda, allowing it to handle varying loads without manual intervention, which is ideal for event-driven architectures. Option C (Offers a pay-per-execution billing model) makes Lambda cost-effective for intermittent workloads, as you only pay for the compute time consumed. Option A (Supports long-running batch jobs exceeding 15 minutes) is incorrect; Lambda functions have a maximum execution duration of 15 minutes, making them unsuitable for long-running batch jobs. Option D (Requires manual provisioning of server infrastructure) is incorrect; Lambda is a serverless service, abstracting away server management. Option E (Optimized for complex, distributed Spark processing) is incorrect; complex Spark processing is better suited for services like AWS Glue or Amazon EMR, not Lambda.

text: Which of the following are benefits of using AWS Step Functions for orchestrating complex data workflows involving AWS Lambda and other services? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Provides built-in retry logic and error handling","Requires manual management of state transitions","Offers visual workflow tracking and debugging","Limited to sequential execution of tasks","Primarily designed for long-running batch ETL jobs on EC2"]
explanation: Option A (Provides built-in retry logic and error handling) is a significant advantage of AWS Step Functions, allowing developers to define how their workflows should react to failures, including automatic retries with backoff strategies. Option C (Offers visual workflow tracking and debugging) provides a graphical console that allows users to visualize the state of their workflows, making it easier to monitor progress and debug issues. Option B (Requires manual management of state transitions) is incorrect; Step Functions automatically manages state transitions between tasks, abstracting away the complexity of coordinating distributed components. Option D (Limited to sequential execution of tasks) is incorrect; Step Functions supports various flow controls, including parallel execution, branching, and dynamic parallelism. Option E (Primarily designed for long-running batch ETL jobs on EC2) is incorrect; while Step Functions can orchestrate ETL, it's serverless and highly flexible, suitable for a wide range of workloads, not just EC2-based batch jobs.

text: A data engineer is writing a Python script for an AWS Glue ETL job. Which of these are good programming practices for ensuring the script is efficient and maintainable? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Hardcoding all configuration parameters directly into the script","Using clear variable names and comments","Implementing proper error handling and logging","Writing a single, very long function for all transformations","Avoiding modularization to keep the code in one file"]
explanation: Option B (Using clear variable names and comments) improves code readability and maintainability, making it easier for other team members (and your future self) to understand and modify the script. Option C (Implementing proper error handling and logging) is crucial for identifying and debugging issues in a data pipeline. Robust error handling prevents job failures and provides insights into data quality problems. Option A (Hardcoding all configuration parameters directly into the script) is an anti-pattern; configurations should be externalized (e.g., using Glue job parameters) to allow for flexibility across environments without modifying code. Option D (Writing a single, very long function for all transformations) is an anti-pattern; it makes the code harder to read, test, and debug. Breaking down complex logic into smaller, focused functions is a best practice. Option E (Avoiding modularization to keep the code in one file) is an anti-pattern; modularization improves code organization, reusability, and testability.

text: When deploying data pipelines using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) with AWS CloudFormation, which benefits are realized? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Manual provisioning of resources for greater control","Version control and change tracking for infrastructure","Consistent and repeatable deployments across environments","Automatic optimization of data processing logic","Elimination of the need for security group configurations"]
explanation: Option B (Version control and change tracking for infrastructure) is a key benefit of IaC. CloudFormation templates can be stored in version control systems, providing a history of changes and enabling easy rollbacks. Option C (Consistent and repeatable deployments across environments) ensures that the same infrastructure configuration can be reliably deployed to development, testing, and production environments, reducing configuration drift and errors. Option A (Manual provisioning of resources for greater control) is incorrect; IaC automates resource provisioning, moving away from manual processes. Option D (Automatic optimization of data processing logic) is incorrect; CloudFormation manages infrastructure, not the optimization of application-level data processing logic. Option E (Elimination of the need for security group configurations) is incorrect; security groups are fundamental for network security, and CloudFormation is used to define and manage them, not eliminate them.

text: A data engineer is tasked with creating a robust CI/CD pipeline for AWS Glue ETL jobs. Which of the following AWS services can be integrated to automate the build, test, and deployment stages of this pipeline? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS CodeCommit","Amazon Kinesis Data Streams","AWS CodeBuild","Amazon Redshift","AWS DataSync"]
explanation: Option A (AWS CodeCommit) is a fully managed source control service that hosts secure Git-based repositories. It's essential for storing the source code of Glue ETL jobs and triggering the CI/CD pipeline upon code changes. Option C (AWS CodeBuild) is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy. It can be used to run unit and integration tests for Glue job scripts. Option B (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams) is a real-time data streaming service, not a CI/CD tool. Option D (Amazon Redshift) is a data warehouse service, not involved in CI/CD orchestration. Option E (AWS DataSync) is a data transfer service used for migrating large amounts of data, not for CI/CD pipelines.

text: A data team needs to automate the deployment of their data pipelines, including AWS Glue jobs, AWS Step Functions, and Amazon S3 buckets. They want to define their infrastructure as code (IaC) to ensure consistency and repeatability across environments. Which two AWS services/tools are best suited for this purpose? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS CloudFormation","AWS CDK (Cloud Development Kit)","AWS Systems Manager","AWS CodePipeline","AWS Lambda"]
explanation: Option A (AWS CloudFormation) allows you to define your AWS infrastructure as code using JSON or YAML templates, enabling consistent and repeatable deployments of services like AWS Glue, Step Functions, and S3. Option B (AWS CDK) is an open-source software development framework that allows you to define your cloud application resources using familiar programming languages. It synthesizes into CloudFormation templates, offering a higher-level abstraction for IaC. Option C (AWS Systems Manager) is for operational tasks like patching, automation, and configuration management, not for defining and deploying infrastructure as code. Option D (AWS CodePipeline) is a continuous delivery service for automating release pipelines, which would use CloudFormation or CDK for deployment but is not the IaC tool itself. Option E (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service, not an IaC tool.

text: A data engineer is developing a serverless data processing application using AWS Lambda. To optimize performance and cost, they need to ensure the Lambda function has sufficient resources for data transformations and can handle a high volume of concurrent invocations. Which two aspects of AWS Lambda configuration are critical for this optimization? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Memory allocation","Provisioned Concurrency","VPC configuration","Execution role permissions","Environment variables"]
explanation: Option A (Memory allocation) directly impacts the CPU and network bandwidth allocated to a Lambda function. Increasing memory can significantly improve the performance of data transformation tasks, which are often CPU and memory-intensive. Option B (Provisioned Concurrency) keeps functions initialized and ready to respond in milliseconds, which is crucial for handling high volumes of concurrent invocations without cold starts, thereby optimizing performance and user experience. Option C (VPC configuration) is important for network access but doesn't directly optimize compute performance or concurrency handling. Option D (Execution role permissions) are essential for the function to interact with other AWS services but don't directly control performance or concurrency. Option E (Environment variables) are for configuration parameters, not for performance or concurrency tuning.

text: A data team is implementing CI/CD for their data pipelines, which consist of AWS Glue jobs and AWS Step Functions workflows. They want to automate the testing and deployment process to ensure reliability and efficiency. Which two benefits does implementing CI/CD provide for this scenario? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Faster release cycles for pipeline updates","Reduced manual errors during deployment","Automatic data validation at source","Simplified data governance policies","Increased data processing throughput"]
explanation: Option A (Faster release cycles for pipeline updates) is a core benefit of CI/CD, as it automates the build, test, and deployment phases, allowing changes to be delivered more quickly and frequently. Option B (Reduced manual errors during deployment) is another key advantage, as automation eliminates human error associated with manual configuration and deployment steps, leading to more reliable deployments. Option C (Automatic data validation at source) is a data quality concern, which CI/CD can help integrate tests for, but it's not a direct benefit of CI/CD itself. Option D (Simplified data governance policies) is related to data management and security, not a direct outcome of CI/CD. Option E (Increased data processing throughput) is a performance characteristic of the data pipeline itself, not a direct benefit of the CI/CD process.

text: When developing AWS Lambda functions for data transformations, a data engineer needs to ensure that the code is version-controlled and can be easily deployed and rolled back. Which two practices are essential for managing Lambda function code in a professional environment? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Using Git for source code management","Packaging deployment artifacts with AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM)","Storing Lambda code directly in Amazon S3","Manually uploading ZIP files via the AWS Management Console","Using AWS CloudTrail for code change auditing"]
explanation: Option A (Using Git for source code management) is fundamental for version control, collaboration, and tracking changes to Lambda function code, enabling easy rollback and branching. Option B (Packaging deployment artifacts with AWS Serverless Application Model (SAM)) provides a framework for defining serverless applications, including Lambda functions, APIs, and databases, as code. SAM templates can be used to package and deploy Lambda functions consistently, supporting CI/CD. Option C (Storing Lambda code directly in Amazon S3) is a step in the deployment process but not a version control system itself. Option D (Manually uploading ZIP files via the AWS Management Console) is an anti-pattern for professional environments as it lacks version control, auditability, and automation. Option E (Using AWS CloudTrail for code change auditing) is for auditing API calls and resource changes, not for managing the source code itself.

text: A data engineer is designing a serverless data pipeline using AWS Step Functions. The pipeline needs to execute a series of tasks, including data validation, transformation, and loading. Which two common state types are fundamental building blocks for defining the logic within an AWS Step Functions state machine? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Task state","Choice state","Start state","End state","Parallel state"]
explanation: Option A (Task state) represents a single unit of work performed by the state machine, such as invoking an AWS Lambda function or an AWS Glue job. This is essential for executing data validation, transformation, and loading steps. Option B (Choice state) allows the state machine to make decisions based on the input, enabling conditional logic to route the workflow down different paths (e.g., based on validation results). Option C (Start state) and Option D (End state) are conceptual entry and exit points, not distinct state types that define logic. Option E (Parallel state) is another fundamental state type for executing multiple branches of a workflow concurrently, but 'Task' and 'Choice' are more foundational for defining sequential and conditional logic.

text: A data engineering team needs to implement a robust CI/CD pipeline for their data transformation jobs, which are built using AWS Glue. The pipeline should automate testing, version control, and deployment. Which two AWS services are commonly used in conjunction with Git for building such a CI/CD pipeline? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS CodePipeline","AWS CodeBuild","AWS CloudFormation","AWS Systems Manager","Amazon EventBridge"]
explanation: Option A (AWS CodePipeline) is a continuous delivery service that automates the build, test, and deploy phases of your release process. It orchestrates the entire pipeline, integrating with other AWS services. Option B (AWS CodeBuild) is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy. It would be used to build and test the AWS Glue job scripts. Option C (AWS CloudFormation) is for defining infrastructure as code, which is deployed by the CI/CD pipeline, but it's not a CI/CD service itself. Option D (AWS Systems Manager) is for operational tasks and configuration management, not for building CI/CD pipelines. Option E (Amazon EventBridge) is for event-driven architectures and scheduling, not a core CI/CD service.

text: A data engineer is optimizing a PySpark script running on AWS Glue. The script performs complex joins and aggregations on large datasets, leading to high shuffle spill and memory pressure. Which two techniques can help improve the performance and stability of this Glue ETL job? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Increasing the number of Data Processing Units (DPUs) for the job","Optimizing data partitioning in Amazon S3 before processing","Reducing the allocated memory for the Glue job","Switching from PySpark to Python Shell for the job","Running the job on a single Amazon EC2 instance"]
explanation: Option A (Increasing the number of Data Processing Units (DPUs) for the job) provides more compute and memory resources to the Glue job, which can alleviate memory pressure and improve performance for complex, resource-intensive operations like joins and aggregations. Option B (Optimizing data partitioning in Amazon S3 before processing) can significantly reduce the amount of data read and shuffled by the Glue job, especially if joins and aggregations are performed on partitioned keys. This is a crucial optimization for distributed processing (ap-1.2-002). Option C (Reducing the allocated memory for the Glue job) would worsen memory pressure and likely lead to more failures or slower performance. Option D (Switching from PySpark to Python Shell for the job) is incorrect; Python Shell jobs are for lightweight tasks and do not support distributed processing like PySpark, which is needed for complex joins on large datasets. Option E (Running the job on a single Amazon EC2 instance) defeats the purpose of using a distributed processing framework like Spark on Glue and would not handle large datasets efficiently.

text: Which AWS services are used for Infrastructure as Code (IaC) to define and deploy AWS resources? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS CloudFormation","AWS CDK","AWS Lambda","AWS Step Functions","Amazon S3"]
explanation: Option A (AWS CloudFormation) is a service that helps you model and set up your AWS resources so you can spend less time managing those resources and more time focusing on your applications running in AWS. Option B (AWS CDK) is an open-source software development framework to define your cloud application resources using familiar programming languages. Both are primary tools for Infrastructure as Code. Option C (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service. Option D (AWS Step Functions) is a serverless workflow orchestration service. Option E (Amazon S3) is an object storage service. These services are not primarily used for defining and deploying infrastructure as code.

text: Which AWS services are specifically designed for orchestrating complex data processing workflows with dependencies and state management? (Select THREE.)
options: ["AWS Step Functions","Amazon MWAA","AWS Glue Workflows","Amazon S3","Amazon CloudWatch"]
explanation: Option A (AWS Step Functions) provides serverless workflow orchestration to coordinate multiple AWS services. Option B (Amazon MWAA) is a managed service for Apache Airflow, enabling complex DAG-based workflows. Option C (AWS Glue Workflows) allows you to create and manage complex ETL pipelines with dependencies between Glue jobs. Option D (Amazon S3) is object storage, and Option E (Amazon CloudWatch) is a monitoring service.

text: Which AWS services enable the creation of serverless and event-driven data processing workflows with minimal operational overhead? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Step Functions","Amazon EventBridge","Amazon EMR","AWS DataSync","Amazon MSK"]
explanation: Option A (AWS Step Functions) provides serverless orchestration for complex workflows, managing state and retries. Option B (Amazon EventBridge) is a serverless event bus that can trigger workflows based on events or schedules, enabling event-driven architectures. Option C (Amazon EMR) is a managed cluster service, Option D (AWS DataSync) is for data transfer, and Option E (Amazon MSK) is a managed Kafka service.

text: Which of the following are advantages of using AWS Step Functions for orchestrating complex, multi-step data ingestion and transformation workflows? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Provides a visual console to track workflow execution state","Requires manual management of task retries and error handling","Supports various control flows like parallel execution and branching","Primarily designed for batch processing on Apache Hadoop clusters","Offers a maximum execution duration of 15 minutes for entire workflows"]
explanation: Option A (Provides a visual console to track workflow execution state) is a significant advantage, allowing users to easily monitor the progress of their workflows, identify bottlenecks, and debug failures through a graphical interface. Option C (Supports various control flows like parallel execution and branching) makes Step Functions highly flexible for complex data pipelines, enabling tasks to run concurrently or conditionally based on previous outcomes. Option B (Requires manual management of task retries and error handling) is incorrect; Step Functions provides built-in mechanisms for defining retry policies and error handling, reducing operational overhead. Option D (Primarily designed for batch processing on Apache Hadoop clusters) is incorrect; Step Functions is serverless and can orchestrate a wide range of AWS services, not just Hadoop-based batch processing. Option E (Offers a maximum execution duration of 15 minutes for entire workflows) is incorrect; Step Functions can orchestrate workflows that run for up to a year, far exceeding the 15-minute limit of individual Lambda functions.

text: A company needs to schedule daily AWS Glue ETL jobs that transform data stored in Amazon S3. Which AWS services can be used to reliably trigger these Glue jobs on a recurring schedule? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Kinesis Data Streams","AWS EventBridge","AWS Step Functions","Amazon SQS","Amazon MSK"]
explanation: Option B (AWS EventBridge) can be used to create scheduled rules (cron-based) that directly trigger AWS Glue jobs or Step Functions workflows, making it ideal for daily recurring tasks. Option C (AWS Step Functions) can orchestrate complex workflows, including scheduling and running AWS Glue jobs as part of a larger process. A Step Functions state machine can be initiated on a schedule via EventBridge. Option A (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams) is for real-time streaming data ingestion, not for scheduling batch jobs. Option D (Amazon SQS) is a message queuing service, used for decoupling applications, not for scheduling. Option E (Amazon MSK) is a managed service for Apache Kafka, used for streaming data, not for scheduling batch ETL jobs.

text: Which of the following AWS services are suitable for building serverless, event-driven data pipelines that react to changes in data (e.g., new files in S3) or scheduled events? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EC2","AWS Lambda","AWS Step Functions","Amazon RDS","Amazon EMR"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Lambda) is a serverless compute service that can be triggered by various events, such as S3 object creation or EventBridge schedules, making it perfect for event-driven data processing. Option C (AWS Step Functions) is a serverless workflow orchestration service that can coordinate multiple Lambda functions and other AWS services, enabling the creation of complex, event-driven data pipelines with built-in error handling and retries. Option A (Amazon EC2) requires manual server management and is not serverless. Option D (Amazon RDS) is a managed relational database service, not a service for building event-driven data pipelines. Option E (Amazon EMR) is a managed cluster platform for big data processing, which is not serverless in the same way as Lambda or Step Functions, and typically used for batch processing rather than event-driven reactions.

text: A data team is migrating an on-premises Apache Airflow environment to AWS to manage their complex data pipelines. Which AWS service is the most appropriate choice for this migration, offering a managed and scalable solution? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Glue Workflows","Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)","AWS Step Functions","AWS Data Pipeline","Amazon EventBridge"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)) is the most direct and appropriate choice as it provides a fully managed service for Apache Airflow, allowing teams to use their existing Airflow DAGs and expertise without managing the underlying infrastructure. Option C (AWS Step Functions) is also a strong contender for orchestrating complex data pipelines, especially if the team wants to move towards a more serverless, state-machine-based approach. While not a direct Airflow migration, it offers similar orchestration capabilities and can be a strategic choice for modernizing. Option A (AWS Glue Workflows) is suitable for orchestrating AWS Glue ETL jobs but is not a general-purpose workflow orchestrator like Airflow or Step Functions. Option D (AWS Data Pipeline) is a legacy service and is generally not recommended for new workloads, especially when migrating from modern orchestrators like Airflow. Option E (Amazon EventBridge) is an event bus service primarily used for routing events and scheduling, not for complex workflow orchestration with dependencies like Airflow.

text: Which of the following AWS services can be used to orchestrate data pipelines and manage dependencies between various data processing tasks, including AWS Glue jobs and AWS Lambda functions? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3","AWS Step Functions","AWS Glue Workflows","Amazon DynamoDB","Amazon Kinesis Data Streams"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Step Functions) is a serverless workflow orchestration service that allows you to define complex, multi-step workflows using state machines. It can easily integrate and manage dependencies between AWS Lambda functions, AWS Glue jobs, and many other AWS services. Option C (AWS Glue Workflows) is specifically designed to orchestrate AWS Glue ETL jobs, crawlers, and other Glue-related tasks, providing dependency management and scheduling capabilities within the Glue ecosystem. Option A (Amazon S3) is an object storage service, not an orchestration service. Option D (Amazon DynamoDB) is a NoSQL database service, not for workflow orchestration. Option E (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams) is a real-time data streaming service, not an orchestration service.

text: Which of the following AWS services can be used to trigger data pipeline components (e.g., AWS Lambda functions or AWS Step Functions) based on a schedule or specific events (e.g., new file uploaded to S3)? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon SQS","Amazon EventBridge","AWS DataSync","Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose","Amazon S3 event notifications"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon EventBridge) allows you to create rules that react to events from AWS services, custom applications, or SaaS applications, and can also trigger targets (like Lambda or Step Functions) based on schedules (cron expressions). Option E (Amazon S3 event notifications) can be configured to send notifications (e.g., to Lambda, SQS, SNS) when specific events occur in an S3 bucket, such as object creation or deletion, making it ideal for triggering pipelines when new data arrives. Option A (Amazon SQS) is a message queuing service, which can be a target for events but doesn't originate schedules or S3 events itself. Option C (AWS DataSync) is a data transfer service, not an event or scheduling service. Option D (Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose) is for ingesting and delivering streaming data, not for triggering based on schedules or S3 events.

text: A data engineer needs to ensure that data pipeline failures are automatically handled with retries and that administrators are notified. Which AWS services can be used to implement automated failure handling and notifications within a data pipeline? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon S3","AWS Step Functions","Amazon SNS","AWS DataSync","Amazon MSK"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Step Functions) provides robust built-in retry logic and error handling mechanisms within its state machine definitions, allowing for automatic retries with configurable backoff strategies. Option C (Amazon SNS) is a messaging service that can be used to send notifications (e.g., email, SMS) to administrators when a Step Functions workflow fails or an AWS Lambda function encounters an error. Option A (Amazon S3) is an object storage service, not for failure handling or notifications. Option D (AWS DataSync) is a data transfer service, not for workflow orchestration or notifications. Option E (Amazon MSK) is a managed Apache Kafka service, used for streaming data, not for general pipeline failure handling or notifications.

text: A data engineer needs to orchestrate a complex, multi-stage data processing workflow that involves several AWS Lambda functions, an AWS Glue job, and a custom containerized application running on Amazon ECS. Which AWS services are best suited for managing the dependencies and state of this workflow? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Data Pipeline","AWS Step Functions","Amazon EventBridge","Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)","Amazon SQS"]
explanation: Option B (AWS Step Functions) is a serverless workflow orchestration service that allows you to define complex workflows as state machines, easily integrating Lambda, Glue, and ECS tasks, and managing their state and dependencies. Option D (Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)) provides a managed Apache Airflow environment, which is a powerful open-source tool for orchestrating complex data pipelines with rich dependency management and scheduling capabilities, suitable for integrating various AWS and custom tasks. Option A (AWS Data Pipeline) is a legacy service and generally not recommended for new complex workflows. Option C (Amazon EventBridge) is an event bus service primarily for routing events and scheduling, but it lacks the sophisticated dependency management and state tracking of Step Functions or MWAA for complex, multi-stage workflows. Option E (Amazon SQS) is a message queuing service used for decoupling components, not for orchestrating entire workflows.

text: Which of the following are benefits of using AWS Glue Workflows for orchestrating data pipelines that primarily consist of AWS Glue jobs and crawlers? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Provides a visual editor for defining job dependencies","Requires manual triggering of each Glue job in sequence","Supports integration with on-premises Apache Airflow environments","Offers built-in monitoring and alerting for workflow execution","Designed for orchestrating non-Glue specific tasks like EC2 instances"]
explanation: Option A (Provides a visual editor for defining job dependencies) is a key feature of AWS Glue Workflows, allowing users to easily define the sequence and dependencies between Glue jobs, crawlers, and other Glue tasks. Option D (Offers built-in monitoring and alerting for workflow execution) integrates with Amazon CloudWatch, providing visibility into the workflow's progress, status, and logs, enabling effective monitoring and alerting. Option B (Requires manual triggering of each Glue job in sequence) is incorrect; Glue Workflows automate the execution and sequencing of jobs based on defined dependencies. Option C (Supports integration with on-premises Apache Airflow environments) is incorrect; while both are orchestrators, Glue Workflows are native to Glue, and MWAA is for managed Airflow. Option E (Designed for orchestrating non-Glue specific tasks like EC2 instances) is incorrect; Glue Workflows are primarily focused on orchestrating tasks within the AWS Glue ecosystem, though they can trigger Lambda functions for broader integration, they are not a general-purpose orchestrator for arbitrary AWS resources like Step Functions or MWAA.

text: A data team is building an event-driven data pipeline. Which AWS services can be used to trigger AWS Lambda functions or AWS Step Functions in response to specific events, such as a new object being created in an Amazon S3 bucket? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Kinesis Data Streams","Amazon S3 event notifications","AWS DataSync","Amazon EventBridge","Amazon MSK"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon S3 event notifications) allows you to configure an S3 bucket to send notifications to target destinations (like AWS Lambda or Amazon SQS) when certain events occur, such as `s3:ObjectCreated:*`. Option D (Amazon EventBridge) can receive events from various AWS services, including S3 (via CloudTrail logs), and then route these events to targets like AWS Lambda functions or AWS Step Functions state machines. Option A (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams) is a real-time data streaming service, not primarily an event trigger for S3 object creation. Option C (AWS DataSync) is a data transfer service, not an event notification service. Option E (Amazon MSK) is a managed Apache Kafka service for streaming data, not for triggering actions based on S3 events.

text: Which of the following are key benefits of using AWS Step Functions for orchestrating serverless data pipelines? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Requires manual management of underlying server infrastructure","Provides built-in state management and visual tracking","Supports long-running workflows (up to a year)","Limited to sequential execution of tasks only","Primarily designed for on-premises workflow orchestration"]
explanation: Option B (Provides built-in state management and visual tracking) is a core benefit of Step Functions, allowing developers to define and monitor complex workflows with a clear visual representation of each step's status. Option C (Supports long-running workflows (up to a year)) is a significant advantage, enabling orchestration of processes that might take hours, days, or even months to complete, which is crucial for many data processing scenarios. Option A (Requires manual management of underlying server infrastructure) is incorrect; Step Functions is a serverless service, abstracting away infrastructure management. Option D (Limited to sequential execution of tasks only) is incorrect; Step Functions supports various control flows, including parallel execution, branching, and dynamic parallelism. Option E (Primarily designed for on-premises workflow orchestration) is incorrect; Step Functions is a cloud-native AWS service designed for orchestrating AWS services.

text: Which of the following are common use cases for AWS EventBridge in the context of data pipelines? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Performing complex, distributed Spark transformations","Scheduling recurring data processing tasks","Routing events from AWS services to targets like Lambda","Storing large volumes of unstructured data","Managing Git repositories for data pipeline code"]
explanation: Option B (Scheduling recurring data processing tasks) is a primary use case for EventBridge, allowing users to define cron-based schedules to trigger AWS Lambda functions, AWS Step Functions, or other targets for daily, hourly, or other periodic data jobs. Option C (Routing events from AWS services to targets like Lambda) is the core functionality of EventBridge. It can receive events from over 200 AWS services and route them to various targets, enabling event-driven architectures for data pipelines. Option A (Performing complex, distributed Spark transformations) is incorrect; this is the domain of services like AWS Glue or Amazon EMR. Option D (Storing large volumes of unstructured data) is incorrect; this is the domain of Amazon S3. Option E (Managing Git repositories for data pipeline code) is incorrect; this is the domain of services like AWS CodeCommit or GitHub.

text: Which of the following are benefits of using Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow) for orchestrating data pipelines compared to a self-managed Airflow instance on EC2? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Requires manual patching and upgrades of Airflow components","Provides automatic scaling of Airflow workers","Offers built-in security and networking configurations","Eliminates the need for DAG development","Limited to orchestrating only AWS Glue jobs"]
explanation: Option B (Provides automatic scaling of Airflow workers) is a key benefit of MWAA, as it automatically scales the underlying compute capacity for Airflow workers based on the workload, reducing operational overhead. Option C (Offers built-in security and networking configurations) simplifies setup and management by integrating with AWS security services (IAM, VPC) and providing secure network configurations out-of-the-box. Option A (Requires manual patching and upgrades of Airflow components) is incorrect; MWAA handles the patching and upgrades of Airflow, reducing operational burden. Option D (Eliminates the need for DAG development) is incorrect; MWAA is a managed service for Airflow, and users still need to develop their DAGs (Directed Acyclic Graphs) to define workflows. Option E (Limited to orchestrating only AWS Glue jobs) is incorrect; MWAA, like open-source Airflow, is a general-purpose orchestrator that can integrate with a wide range of services, both AWS and non-AWS.

text: Which of the following are anti-patterns for data pipeline orchestration that managed AWS services aim to address? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Using AWS Step Functions for serverless workflows","Building custom cron-based schedulers on EC2 instances","Leveraging AWS Glue Workflows for ETL job dependencies","Implementing manual retry logic for transient failures","Relying on complex shell scripts for task sequencing"]
explanation: Option B (Building custom cron-based schedulers on EC2 instances) is an anti-pattern (`ap-1.3-001`). Custom schedulers require significant operational overhead for infrastructure management, failure handling, monitoring, and scaling. Managed services like MWAA or EventBridge provide these capabilities out-of-the-box. Option E (Relying on complex shell scripts for task sequencing) is also an anti-pattern. While shell scripts can perform tasks, managing complex dependencies, error handling, state, and monitoring across multiple scripts becomes difficult and brittle. Managed orchestrators offer structured, observable, and resilient ways to define workflows. Option A (Using AWS Step Functions for serverless workflows) is a best practice, not an anti-pattern. Option C (Leveraging AWS Glue Workflows for ETL job dependencies) is a best practice for Glue-centric pipelines. Option D (Implementing manual retry logic for transient failures) is generally an anti-pattern if it's truly manual; managed services offer automated and configurable retry mechanisms.

text: A company requires a robust and scalable solution to schedule and manage hundreds of daily data processing jobs, including Spark jobs on Amazon EMR and custom Python scripts. The solution needs to support complex dependencies, backfilling, and integrate with existing CI/CD pipelines. Which two AWS services are best suited for this orchestration challenge? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)","AWS Step Functions","AWS Glue Workflows","Amazon EventBridge","AWS Lambda"]
explanation: Option A (Amazon MWAA) provides a fully managed Apache Airflow environment, which is highly capable of orchestrating complex data pipelines with hundreds of jobs, managing dependencies, supporting backfilling, and integrating well with CI/CD. Option B (AWS Step Functions) is a serverless workflow orchestration service that can define complex, stateful workflows, including invoking Amazon EMR steps and AWS Lambda functions for custom Python scripts. It offers robust error handling and visual tracking. Option C (AWS Glue Workflows) is excellent for orchestrating AWS Glue jobs but might be less flexible for managing a diverse set of jobs like EMR Spark jobs and arbitrary Python scripts across different compute environments. Option D (Amazon EventBridge) is primarily for event-driven triggers and scheduling, not for managing complex dependencies or backfilling. Option E (AWS Lambda) is a compute service for individual tasks, not an orchestration service for entire pipelines.

text: A data pipeline needs to be triggered based on a schedule (e.g., daily at midnight) and also in response to specific events (e.g., a new file upload to S3). The pipeline involves invoking AWS Lambda functions and AWS Glue jobs. Which two AWS services can be used to reliably trigger these components? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon EventBridge","AWS Step Functions","AWS Data Pipeline","Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)","Amazon Kinesis Data Streams"]
explanation: Option A (Amazon EventBridge) is excellent for schedule-based triggers (using cron expressions) and event-driven triggers (reacting to events from S3, Lambda, or other AWS services). It can directly invoke AWS Lambda functions and start AWS Step Functions workflows. Option B (AWS Step Functions) can be started by EventBridge or S3 events and can orchestrate a series of Lambda functions and Glue jobs, providing state management and retry logic. Option D (Amazon MWAA) is a powerful orchestration service that can handle schedules and complex dependencies but might be overkill for simple event-driven triggers. Option C (AWS Data Pipeline) is a legacy service and is deprecated. Option E (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams) is for real-time data ingestion, not for pipeline orchestration or scheduling.

text: A data team is building a serverless data pipeline that needs to execute a sequence of AWS Lambda functions and potentially long-running AWS Glue jobs. The pipeline requires robust error handling, state management, and the ability to pause and resume. Which two AWS services provide these orchestration capabilities? (Select TWO.)
options: ["AWS Step Functions","AWS Glue Workflows","Amazon EventBridge","AWS Data Pipeline","AWS Lambda"]
explanation: Option A (AWS Step Functions) is a serverless workflow orchestration service that excels at managing state, providing robust error handling, retries, and the ability to pause and resume workflows. It can orchestrate Lambda functions and Glue jobs. Option B (AWS Glue Workflows) is specifically designed to orchestrate AWS Glue jobs and other AWS services, offering dependency management, scheduling, and monitoring, including error handling and retries for Glue jobs. Option C (Amazon EventBridge) is for event-driven triggers and scheduling, not for complex workflow orchestration with state management. Option D (AWS Data Pipeline) is a legacy service and is deprecated. Option E (AWS Lambda) is a compute service for individual tasks, not an orchestration service that manages the state and flow of multiple interdependent steps.

text: A data engineering team needs to build a highly scalable and fault-tolerant data pipeline that processes real-time data streams. The pipeline must ensure data delivery to multiple downstream systems and allow for custom processing logic. Which two AWS services are fundamental for building such a resilient streaming ingestion and processing architecture? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Kinesis Data Streams","AWS Lambda","Amazon S3","Amazon EventBridge","AWS DataSync"]
explanation: Option A (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams) provides a highly scalable and fault-tolerant way to capture and store large streams of data records, enabling multiple consumers to process the data in real-time. Option B (AWS Lambda) can be directly invoked by Kinesis Data Streams to apply custom processing logic to the streaming data, providing serverless, scalable compute for transformations and routing to downstream systems. Option C (Amazon S3) is a destination for processed data but not an ingestion or processing service itself. Option D (Amazon EventBridge) is for event routing and scheduling, not for continuous streaming data ingestion or processing. Option E (AWS DataSync) is for large-scale data transfer from on-premises to AWS, not for real-time streaming pipelines.

text: A data team needs to ensure that their data pipelines are resilient to failures and can automatically recover from transient errors. They are using AWS Step Functions to orchestrate a series of AWS Lambda functions. Which two features of AWS Step Functions help achieve this resilience? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Built-in retry mechanisms","Error handling with Catch states","Automatic scaling of Lambda functions","Data validation at the source","Version control for state machines"]
explanation: Option A (Built-in retry mechanisms) allow Step Functions to automatically retry failed steps, which is crucial for handling transient errors and improving pipeline resilience. Option B (Error handling with Catch states) enables defining specific actions to take when an error occurs in a state, such as falling back to a different path or notifying operators, thus providing robust error management. Option C (Automatic scaling of Lambda functions) is a feature of Lambda itself, not Step Functions, although Step Functions orchestrates Lambda. Option D (Data validation at the source) is a data quality concern, not a resilience feature of Step Functions. Option E (Version control for state machines) is important for development and deployment but doesn't directly contribute to runtime resilience or automatic recovery.

text: A data engineering team is migrating legacy batch processing jobs from on-premises servers to AWS. These jobs involve complex dependencies and require a managed orchestration service that supports Python and can be easily integrated with existing CI/CD pipelines. Which two AWS services are ideal for this migration? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon MWAA (Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow)","AWS Step Functions","AWS Glue Workflows","AWS Data Pipeline","Amazon EventBridge"]
explanation: Option A (Amazon MWAA) provides a fully managed Apache Airflow environment, which is highly suitable for migrating complex batch processing jobs with intricate dependencies. It supports Python-based DAGs and integrates well with CI/CD. Option B (AWS Step Functions) is a serverless workflow orchestration service that can define complex, stateful workflows, including invoking AWS Glue jobs or AWS Lambda functions for Python scripts. It offers robust error handling and visual tracking, making it suitable for modernizing batch jobs. Option C (AWS Glue Workflows) is primarily for orchestrating AWS Glue jobs and might be less flexible for managing a broader range of legacy jobs. Option D (AWS Data Pipeline) is a legacy service and is deprecated in favor of Glue Workflows or MWAA. Option E (Amazon EventBridge) is for event-driven triggers and scheduling, not for managing complex job dependencies and orchestration.

text: Which AWS services are specifically designed for orchestrating complex data pipelines and managing job dependencies? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Kinesis Data Streams","Amazon MWAA","Amazon S3","AWS Glue Workflows","AWS DMS"]
explanation: Option B (Amazon MWAA) is a managed orchestration service for Apache Airflow that helps you manage and execute data pipelines. It provides built-in retry policies, dependency management, and monitoring for complex workflows. Option D (AWS Glue Workflows) allows you to create and run multi-job ETL pipelines, managing dependencies between different AWS Glue jobs, crawlers, and other services. Option A (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams) is for real-time data ingestion. Option C (Amazon S3) is an object storage service. Option E (AWS DMS) is for database migration and change data capture, not general pipeline orchestration.

text: Which AWS services are suitable for large-scale batch data ingestion from various sources into Amazon S3? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Kinesis Data Streams","AWS DataSync","Amazon MSK","AWS Glue","AWS DMS"]
explanation: Option B (AWS DataSync) is designed for large-scale online data transfer from on-premises to AWS, often into Amazon S3, supporting various file systems and storage types. Option D (AWS Glue) can ingest data from various sources (like databases, S3) in batch for ETL jobs. Option A (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams) and Option C (Amazon MSK) are for streaming data. Option E (AWS DMS) is primarily for database migration and continuous data replication, not general batch file ingestion.

text: A financial institution needs to ingest high-volume, real-time transaction data from various sources into its AWS data lake for immediate fraud detection and analytics. The data arrives continuously, with peak rates of hundreds of thousands of records per second, and requires sub-second latency processing. The solution must be fully managed, scalable, and support integration with downstream analytics services. (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to capture and store the real-time data.","Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) to provide a fully managed Kafka-compatible streaming platform.","AWS DataSync to transfer data from on-premises sources to Amazon S3.","Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to buffer and deliver data directly to Amazon Redshift.","AWS Glue batch ETL jobs to process incoming data files every 5 minutes."]
explanation: Option A (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams) is correct because it is a highly scalable and durable real-time data streaming service capable of ingesting hundreds of thousands of records per second with sub-second latency, making it ideal for immediate fraud detection. Option B (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK)) is also correct as it provides a fully managed, highly available, and scalable Apache Kafka service, suitable for high-volume real-time data ingestion and compatible with existing Kafka applications. Option C (AWS DataSync) is incorrect as it is designed for large-scale, online data transfer from on-premises to AWS, not for real-time streaming ingestion. Option D (Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose) is incorrect because while it can ingest streaming data, its primary purpose is buffering and delivering to destinations like Amazon S3 or Redshift, which might introduce more latency than required for 'immediate' fraud detection compared to Kinesis Data Streams or MSK directly. Option E (AWS Glue batch ETL jobs) is incorrect as using batch ingestion for real-time analytics requirements is an anti-pattern, as it introduces latency proportional to batch size and frequency, failing the sub-second latency requirement.

text: A company plans to migrate an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and needs to continuously replicate ongoing changes from the source database to the target with minimal downtime. Additionally, they want to capture these change data records for historical analysis in an Amazon S3 data lake. The solution must be robust, managed, and support both initial load and continuous replication. (Select TWO.)
options: ["Configure AWS DMS to perform a full load and ongoing change data capture (CDC) from Oracle to Amazon RDS.","Set up Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to receive CDC events from AWS DMS and deliver them to an Amazon S3 bucket.","Utilize AWS Glue ETL jobs to periodically query the Oracle database for new records and update Amazon S3.","Implement AWS DataSync to transfer database backups from on-premises to Amazon S3 for archival.","Deploy Amazon MSK to stream database logs directly from the on-premises Oracle database."]
explanation: Option A (Configure AWS DMS to perform a full load and ongoing change data capture (CDC) from Oracle to Amazon RDS) is correct because AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) is specifically designed for migrating databases with minimal downtime and performing continuous CDC, supporting various source and target endpoints including Oracle and Amazon RDS. Option B (Set up Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to receive CDC events from AWS DMS and deliver them to an Amazon S3 bucket) is also correct. AWS DMS can stream CDC events to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, which can then be delivered to Amazon S3 via Kinesis Data Firehose, enabling historical analysis in a data lake. Option C (Utilize AWS Glue ETL jobs to periodically query the Oracle database) is incorrect as this approach is not suitable for continuous, low-latency CDC and would likely involve higher operational overhead and latency compared to DMS. Option D (Implement AWS DataSync to transfer database backups) is incorrect because DataSync is for file system and object storage migration, not for continuous database CDC. Option E (Deploy Amazon MSK to stream database logs) is incorrect as directly streaming database logs from Oracle to MSK for CDC is a complex, custom implementation that lacks the managed capabilities and specific CDC features of AWS DMS.

text: A large enterprise needs to migrate 500 TB of archival data stored on network file shares in their on-premises data center to Amazon S3. The migration must be secure, efficient, and minimize the impact on network bandwidth for other business operations. The data needs to be moved over a period of weeks, not months, and the process should be easily manageable. (Select TWO.)
options: ["Use AWS DataSync to automate and accelerate the online transfer of data from on-premises to Amazon S3.","Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the target Amazon S3 bucket to speed up long-distance data transfers.","Deploy an Amazon EMR cluster on-premises to copy data to Amazon S3 using distributed processing.","Implement a custom script on an Amazon EC2 instance to periodically sync data to Amazon S3.","Utilize Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the archival data directly from the network file shares."]
explanation: Option A (Use AWS DataSync to automate and accelerate the online transfer of data from on-premises to Amazon S3) is correct because AWS DataSync is a managed service specifically designed for large-scale, online data transfers between on-premises storage and AWS services like Amazon S3, ensuring efficiency, security, and manageability. Option B (Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the target Amazon S3 bucket to speed up long-distance data transfers) is also correct as it uses Amazon CloudFront's globally distributed edge locations to accelerate data transfers to and from S3 buckets, which would significantly reduce the time needed for a 500 TB migration over weeks. Option C (Deploy an Amazon EMR cluster on-premises) is incorrect as EMR is a distributed processing framework, not a primary service for large-scale file migration from on-premises. Option D (Implement a custom script on an Amazon EC2 instance) is incorrect because custom solutions lack the managed features, reliability, and optimization of AWS DataSync, increasing operational overhead and potential for errors. Option E (Utilize Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the archival data) is incorrect as Kinesis Data Firehose is for streaming data ingestion, typically for smaller, continuous data flows, not for large-scale batch migration of archival files from network shares.

text: A mobile application generates small, frequent events (e.g., user clicks, impressions) that need to be ingested into a data pipeline for real-time analytics. The solution must be serverless, highly scalable to handle millions of events per hour, and provide an API endpoint for the mobile clients to send data directly. The ingested data will then be processed by a streaming service. (Select TWO.)
options: ["Amazon API Gateway to expose a secure, scalable API endpoint for mobile clients.","Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to capture and store the high-volume, real-time event data.","AWS Glue ETL jobs triggered by Amazon EventBridge to process events in batches.","Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to quickly upload individual event files to a bucket.","AWS DataSync to periodically transfer event logs from mobile devices to Amazon S3."]
explanation: Option A (Amazon API Gateway to expose a secure, scalable API endpoint for mobile clients) is correct because API Gateway is a fully managed service that allows developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs at any scale, making it ideal for mobile clients to send events. Option B (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to capture and store the high-volume, real-time event data) is also correct as it is a highly scalable and durable real-time data streaming service that can handle millions of events per hour with low latency, perfectly fitting the requirement for a streaming service to process the ingested data. Option C (AWS Glue ETL jobs triggered by Amazon EventBridge) is incorrect as batch processing is unsuitable for real-time analytics requirements. Option D (Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration) is incorrect because while it speeds up S3 uploads, it's not designed for direct API-based ingestion of small, frequent events, nor does it provide the streaming processing capabilities. Option E (AWS DataSync) is incorrect as DataSync is for large-scale data migration between storage systems, not for real-time API-based event ingestion from mobile applications.

text: A data engineering team is designing a new pipeline to collect sensor data from IoT devices. The requirement is to provide near real-time dashboards (sub-second latency) for operational monitoring and anomaly detection. The team is considering different ingestion approaches. Which of the following approaches would be MOST suitable for meeting the real-time requirements, while avoiding common anti-patterns? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Ingest data into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for immediate processing by a downstream consumer.","Utilize Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) to build a scalable, low-latency streaming platform.","Configure AWS Glue batch ETL jobs to run every 15 minutes to process new sensor data.","Use AWS DataSync to transfer sensor data files from edge devices to Amazon S3 once per hour.","Implement Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration for direct uploads of sensor data files to Amazon S3."]
explanation: Option A (Ingest data into Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for immediate processing by a downstream consumer) is correct because Kinesis Data Streams is designed for real-time data ingestion and processing with sub-second latency, directly meeting the requirement for near real-time dashboards and anomaly detection. Option B (Utilize Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) to build a scalable, low-latency streaming platform) is also correct as MSK provides a fully managed Apache Kafka service, which is a robust, scalable, and low-latency streaming platform suitable for real-time data processing and analytics. Option C (Configure AWS Glue batch ETL jobs to run every 15 minutes) is incorrect because using batch ingestion for real-time analytics requirements is an anti-pattern (ap-1.1-001); a 15-minute batch interval introduces significant latency, failing the sub-second requirement. Option D (Use AWS DataSync to transfer sensor data files) is incorrect as DataSync is for large-scale file transfers, not real-time streaming data ingestion. Option E (Implement Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration for direct uploads) is incorrect because while it speeds up S3 uploads, it's still a file-based approach, and processing files from S3 would not meet sub-second latency requirements for real-time dashboards.

text: A data analytics team needs to ingest high-volume clickstream data from a website for real-time analytics and store it in Amazon Redshift. They are looking for an efficient and cost-effective method to load the streaming data into Redshift, ensuring that data is available for queries within minutes. Which of the following approaches represent best practices for loading streaming data into Amazon Redshift? (Select TWO.)
options: ["Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to automatically deliver streaming data to Amazon S3, then use Redshift COPY commands.","Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to directly stream data into Amazon Redshift with automated batching.","Implement AWS DMS to capture clickstream events and replicate them to Amazon Redshift.","Develop custom AWS Lambda functions to insert individual clickstream records into Redshift.","Utilize AWS Glue ETL jobs to periodically read from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and load into Redshift."]
explanation: Option A (Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to automatically deliver streaming data to Amazon S3, then use Redshift COPY commands) is correct. This is a best practice for efficient and cost-effective loading of streaming data into Redshift. Kinesis Data Firehose buffers data and delivers it to S3, from where Redshift's `COPY` command can perform highly optimized bulk loading. Option B (Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to directly stream data into Amazon Redshift with automated batching) is also correct. Kinesis Data Firehose supports direct streaming ingestion into Redshift, performing automated batching and optimizing the load process, which is an efficient method to get data into Redshift quickly.
